newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Fidelity's Irish arm to create 400 jobs in Dublin.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity's Irish arm to create 400 jobs in Dublin.

text.p: U.S. financial services group Fidelity Investments said on Wednesday it was establishing a technology centre in Dublin leading to 400 new jobs.

"This is a major coup for Dublin, attracting a leading edge company that is managing assets the equivalent of eight times Ireland's GNP," enterprise and employment minister Richard Bruton said in a statement.

Bruton said the Fidelity Ireland operation, which would be involved in advanced technology and software development, would employ 260 highly skilled people within three years and build up its workforce to 400 within five years.
"We are targeting the world's top 100 financial services companies with a view to their establising back office type operations in Ireland," Bruton said.

The Irish financial services sector has the potential to generate at least 5,000 jobs over the short to medium term and has already attracted international companies like Merrill Lynch, Bankers Trust and Whirlpool, he said.
